# 3. Project Overview

**Close friendships often become more difficult to maintain** after graduation, relocation, or other periods of physical separation. Although social media provides a convenient way to remain aware of one another's lives, most platforms are built around immediate publishing, public visibility, and continuous engagement. In practice, this often encourages users to share only selected or highly curated moments rather than the small, ordinary experiences that make up everyday life.

Rewind is proposed as a private, cross-platform social-memory application designed to address this problem. Instead of operating as an instant social feed, Rewind allows members of a close friend group to contribute short, candid video moments to a shared time capsule over a fixed period. Contributions remain inaccessible after submission. At the end of the cycle, Rewind automatically combines the group's clips into a chronological film and reveals it to all members as a shared event.

**Rewind is intentionally not a public social network and not a camera-filter catalogue.** It has no public feed, follower system, hashtags, discovery, or public profiles. Its engineering value lies in coordinating private membership, timed state transitions, contribution policies, locked media, asynchronous media processing, reliable reveal, notifications, chat, secure storage, and failure recovery. Retro processing supports the product experience, but the defining workflow is the private group time capsule.

Expected benefits of the proposed system include:

- **More genuine group connection**: delayed reveal reduces the pressure to curate or perform for immediate reactions and gives geographically separated friends a recurring shared event.

- Reliable shared-memory creation: media is validated, processed, ordered, compiled, archived, and exposed through explicit lifecycle states with retry and failure handling.

- **A structured and consistent contribution process:** Contribution limits, timing rules, deletion allowances, and reveal behaviour are enforced by the system rather than depending on informal agreement between group members.

# Functional Requirements

## 4.1 Identity, Private Groups, and Invitations

This module establishes the trust boundary for Rewind. All group content is private and may be accessed only by authenticated members of the relevant group.

**Authentication:** Users shall authenticate through a standards-based OpenID Connect flow. The preferred implementation is Amazon Cognito User Pools acting as the managed OIDC provider so that Rewind does not implement password storage or credential verification itself.

**Group Creation:** An authenticated user may create an invite-only group. The creator becomes the group owner and may set the group name and prompt configuration. The MVP supports groups of 2–10 members.

**Invitations:** The owner may create expiring invitation links. A link shall open the native application when available and otherwise direct the user to the web/PWA flow. Joining requires authentication and server-side validation of the invite and group capacity.

**Authorization:** The backend shall verify group membership for all operations involving group metadata, chat, clips, films, prompts, and downloads. Signed media URLs shall be issued only after this authorization check.

**MVP Membership Boundary:** Owner transfer, member removal, leaving groups, and account-deletion workflows are outside the first delivery. Their absence will be documented as a privacy and retention limitation rather than treated as complete production functionality.

## 4.2 Capture, Retro Processing, and Contribution Control

This module controls how media enters the system and enforces the product constraint that contributions are short, intentional, and unavailable for repeated review before reveal.

**Camera-First Capture:** The application shall open to an in-app video camera. Normal MVP contributions shall be recorded inside Rewind; gallery import may be enabled only in development or test builds for repeatable demonstrations.

**Capture Format:** The MVP shall record vertical 720p video with source audio. A single clip may be at most 15 seconds. The user may trim the recorded clip before submission.

**Retro Modes:** The client shall provide a small set of original retro-inspired processing modes. The working MVP set is disposable-flash, compact-digital/CCD, 8mm home-movie, and VHS/camcorder aesthetics. Effects will be original implementations inspired by broad visual conventions rather than copies of another application’s assets, names, interface, or filter recipes.

**Post-Capture Processing:** The retro treatment shall be applied after recording and before final upload. A real-time GPU filter preview is not required for the MVP.

**Weekly Budget:** For each seven-day window measured from the cycle start date, each member may submit no more than five clips and no more than 30 seconds of combined video. The server shall validate both limits before accepting a contribution.

**Locked Contribution:** After successful submission, the contributor shall not be able to replay the clip or view a thumbnail. The application shall expose only non-content metadata such as the number of clips submitted and seconds used.

**Single Correction:** A member may delete one contributed clip per weekly window before the applicable cutoff. Deletion restores the associated clip-count and duration budget, permitting a replacement capture.

## 4.3 Cycle, Reveal, and Archive Lifecycle

The group cycle is the core domain lifecycle. It determines when contributions are accepted, when compilation starts, when the film becomes visible, and when the next cycle begins.

**Cycle Duration:** The production default shall be four weeks from the group start date. The duration shall be configurable so that a one-day cycle can be used in the test and demonstration environment.

**Cycle State:** The backend shall maintain an explicit state for each cycle, including capture, processing, reveal, and archived states. Time-based transitions shall be performed server-side rather than relying on a client device remaining active.

**Automatic Rollover:** At the cycle boundary, new submissions to the closing cycle shall stop, compilation shall begin, and the next capture cycle shall start immediately so that the group does not lose its regular capture rhythm.

**Reveal Window:** When compilation succeeds, the group film shall premiere in a 24-hour reveal period. The film remains permanently accessible from the group archive after the premiere window ends.

## 4.4 Automatic Film Compilation

This module converts individually submitted clips into a deterministic shared artifact. Compilation is asynchronous because video validation, audio processing, concatenation, and storage may exceed normal interactive request times.

**Ordered Assembly:** The compiler shall assemble accepted clips in chronological order. The resulting film may be visually segmented by day without requiring the application to expose a separate pre-reveal day-by-day media feed.

**Media Validation:** Before assembly, each clip shall be checked for expected format, orientation, duration, and media readability. Invalid or missing inputs shall fail safely and be surfaced through job status rather than producing a corrupt final film.

**Audio Handling:** Source audio shall be preserved and volume-normalized across the compiled film. Licensed background music is excluded from the MVP.

**Low-Contribution Filler:** If the group film does not meet its baseline duration, the compiler may reuse a prior memory associated with the relevant member; if none is available, a past group memory may be selected. Reused media must carry the archive label. The exact repeat-selection rule remains an implementation decision.

**Retry and Failure State:** Compilation jobs shall retry automatically for transient failures. After a bounded number of retries, the group shall be informed that the film is delayed and the system shall expose a safe, recoverable processing status instead of silently failing.

**Output:** On success, the final group film shall be written to private cloud storage, associated with the completed cycle, and made available only to authorized group members through short-lived access URLs.

## 4.5 Prompts and Reminders

Prompts and reminders encourage participation without becoming the central product. Their configuration is intentionally simple for the first release.

**Prompts:** The application shall provide built-in prompts. The group owner may select a built-in prompt or provide a short custom prompt for the group.

**Default Reminder:** The default reminder shall be delivered once per week on Sunday at 7:00 p.m. in the group’s configured local time.

**Member Preference:** A member may snooze or disable the reminder. Notification preferences shall not alter the server-side contribution deadlines or cycle state.

**Delivery Handling:** Notification requests shall be handled asynchronously. Provider responses, invalid device tokens, and retryable delivery failures shall be recorded so that notification failure does not block core group operations.

## 4.6 Private Group Chat

Each private group shall include a lightweight real-time conversation space to support discussion around the shared experience without turning Rewind into a general-purpose messaging platform.

**Messaging:** Members shall be able to send text messages within groups they belong to.

**Conversation Features:** The MVP shall support reactions and replies. Typing indicators, read receipts, arbitrary file attachments, message editing, and message deletion are deferred.

**Two-Person Groups:** A two-person group shall cover the direct-message use case; a separate private-message product is not required.

**Access Control:** Chat history and real-time events shall use the same authenticated group-membership checks as the rest of the application.

## 4.7 Playback, Download, and Personal Access

**Film Playback:** Authorized members shall be able to play the revealed group film during the reveal window and from the permanent group archive afterwards.

**Group Film Download:** After reveal, members may download the completed group film.

**Own Clip Download:** After reveal, a member may download their own processed clips. Pre-reveal access remains prohibited.

**Processed-Media Retention:** The cloud shall retain only the processed retro-styled media required for the product workflow. Original unfiltered uploads shall be deleted after processing succeeds.

# 5. Non-Functional Requirements

The following quality targets are defined for the bounded academic deployment and five-person acceptance scenario. Media-processing operations are intentionally measured separately from normal interactive API requests.

## 5.1 Performance and Responsiveness

**Interactive API Response:** Under the acceptance-test workload, non-media API operations such as group retrieval, prompt updates, contribution-budget checks, and chat-history retrieval should complete within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile, excluding external identity-provider latency.

**Direct Media Transfer:** Large media bytes shall not pass through the main application API. The backend shall issue short-lived, narrowly scoped upload/download URLs so that the client transfers media directly to private object storage.

**Compilation Target:** For the synthetic five-member demonstration group, a cycle containing at most 25 new clips and at most 150 seconds of contributed video should compile within 10 minutes under normal test conditions. This is a project acceptance target, not a commercial-scale SLA.

## 5.2 Security and Privacy

**Managed Identity:** Authentication shall use OIDC and short-lived application tokens. The application shall not store plaintext user passwords.

**Least Privilege:** Cloud services, CI/CD identities, and media-processing components shall receive only the permissions required for their role. Private media storage shall not be publicly readable.

**Transport and Storage:** Client-to-service traffic shall use HTTPS. Sensitive configuration and credentials shall be stored outside source code. Cloud storage and managed data services shall use provider-supported encryption at rest.

**Authorization Tests:** Automated integration tests shall cover attempts to read or mutate another group’s data, request another group’s media URL, or exceed contribution policy.

**Data Minimization:** Original unfiltered uploads shall be removed after successful processing; only processed clips and derived group films required for the product workflow shall remain.

## 5.3 Reliability and Recoverability

**Idempotent Jobs:** Scheduled cycle transitions and compilation tasks shall be safe to retry so that duplicate scheduler delivery does not create multiple films or corrupt state.

**Durable Job Status:** Compilation and notification work shall have explicit persisted states that can be inspected after process restarts or transient cloud failures.

**Graceful Failure:** Failed compilation shall not expose incomplete media as a successful reveal. The UI shall show a delayed/processing state while bounded retries or operator recovery are performed.

**Backup:** Relational application data shall be backed up using the selected managed database backup mechanism. Media will reside in private object storage with versioning or recovery settings chosen according to project cost constraints.

## 5.4 Usability and Accessibility

**Capture Simplicity:** A signed-in group member should be able to open the camera, record, trim, and submit a clip without navigating through a public feed or media library.

**Clear Constraints:** The capture UI shall show remaining clip count and available seconds and shall explain why a submission is rejected when a budget or timing rule is exceeded.

**State Visibility:** Processing, reveal, archive, notification, and failure states shall use explicit user-facing status messages rather than silent transitions.

## 5.5 Maintainability and Testability

**Modular Boundaries:** Domain logic for membership, contribution policy, cycle state, media jobs, notifications, and chat shall be separated behind clear interfaces within a modular backend.

**Automated Testing:** Core contribution limits, authorization rules, lifecycle transitions, ordering, retry behaviour, and API contracts shall be covered by automated unit and integration tests. End-to-end smoke tests shall exercise the capture-to-reveal vertical slice.

**Configuration:** Cycle duration, contribution limits used in test environments, reminder scheduling, and media-processing choices shall be configuration rather than hard-coded environment assumptions where practical.

**Observability:** The deployed system shall record structured logs and operational metrics for API errors, job failures, compilation duration, notification failures, and scheduled transition outcomes.

## 5.6 Portability and Deployment

**Cross-Platform Client:** The primary client shall target Android and iOS from a shared React Native/Expo codebase. The same codebase shall also produce an installable web/PWA build where platform capability permits.

**Release Target:** The project intends to produce an Android APK, an iOS build or preview subject to developer-account/signing access, and an installable PWA. Public App Store approval is not an acceptance criterion for the academic project.

**Cloud Deployment:** Backend services shall be deployable to AWS using repeatable environment configuration. The architecture shall prioritize low prototype cost rather than commercial-scale redundancy.

# 6. General Architecture

The proposed solution uses a mobile-first client, a modular cloud backend, private object storage, a relational database, and asynchronous workers for work that cannot safely be performed inside an interactive request. The architecture deliberately separates control-plane operations (identity, rules, state, metadata) from the media data path.

| **Component**         | **Responsibility**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Client                | React Native / Expo application for iOS and Android; web/PWA build from the same codebase. Provides camera capture, trim, retro processing, group/chat/reveal UI, local notification token handling, and authenticated HTTPS calls.                                                                           |
| Identity              | Amazon Cognito User Pools as the preferred OIDC provider. The API validates issued tokens and applies group-level authorization.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Application API       | A modular backend responsible for groups, invitations, membership, prompts, contribution budgets, cycle/reveal state, chat metadata/events, signed media access, scheduling, and audit-relevant state.                                                                                                        |
| Relational Data       | PostgreSQL for users/profile references, groups, memberships, invitations, cycles, contribution metadata, prompts, notification preferences, chat records, and processing state.                                                                                                                              |
| Media Storage         | Private Amazon S3 bucket. The API issues short-lived scoped URLs for upload and authorized download; the bucket is never public.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Media Processing      | Asynchronous worker using either AWS Elemental MediaConvert or a containerized FFmpeg pipeline after a prototype comparison. Responsibilities include validation/transcode, retro-processed media handling, audio normalization, chronological concatenation, archive filler handling, and final-film output. |
| Scheduling / Jobs     | Server-side scheduled jobs close cycles, start compilation, retry transient failures, publish reveal state, and issue reminders. Jobs are designed to be idempotent.                                                                                                                                          |
| Notifications         | Expo Push Notifications as a cross-platform delivery interface to APNs/FCM, with token cleanup, failure logging, and retry where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Delivery / Operations | Source control, CI quality and security checks, containerized backend components, infrastructure/configuration automation, staged deployment, structured logging, metrics, and smoke tests.                                                                                                                   |

# 7. Scope of Work

## 7.1 MVP Scope

- Cross-platform sign-in using managed OIDC identity.

- Creation of invite-only groups with 2–10 members and expiring invitation links.

- Group-owner controls for group name and built-in/custom prompts.

- In-app vertical 720p video capture, trimming, and a small set of original retro-inspired post-capture effects.

- Weekly contribution limits: five clips, 15 seconds maximum per clip, 30 seconds combined, with a single deletion-and-retake allowance.

- Locked pre-reveal media with metadata-only contribution feedback.

- Configurable cycle duration with four weeks as the product default and one day for test/demo.

- Server-side cycle transitions, automatic compilation, 24-hour reveal, permanent group archive, and immediate start of the next cycle.

- Chronological film assembly with source audio normalization, bounded retry, safe delayed status, and labelled archive filler.

- Weekly prompts/reminders with snooze/disable preference.

- Private group chat with text, reactions, and replies.

- Post-reveal playback and download of group films and a member’s own processed clips.

- Private cloud storage, relational persistence, CI/CD, automated tests, deployment, logging, and operational evidence.

- Android APK, iOS build/preview subject to signing access, and installable PWA output from the shared client codebase.

## 7.3 Explicit Exclusions / Acceptance Boundaries

The proposal does not claim commercial-scale availability, massive media storage, public-content moderation, licensed background music, guaranteed push-delivery timing, or App Store review approval. These would materially expand the project beyond the intended academic scope.

# 8. Effort Estimates

The work is planned across four major iterations over approximately ten weeks, matching the staged-delivery style used in the project proposal references. The sequence prioritizes a thin end-to-end vertical slice before optional camera or UI polish so that the highest-risk lifecycle and media path is proven early.

| **Iteration** | **Duration** | **Activities**                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **Deliverables**                                                                                                                                                          |
|---------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1             | 2 weeks      | Requirements refinement; use cases and domain model; architecture baseline; repository/CI setup; OIDC sign-in; group creation/invite/membership; initial database and private storage; deployable staging skeleton.     | Approved requirements baseline; analysis/design artefacts; working authentication and private-group flow; CI pipeline; staging deployment.                                |
| 2             | 3 weeks      | Camera capture/trim; retro post-processing; signed upload path; contribution metadata; weekly count/duration rules; locked media; correction allowance; configurable cycle state and scheduler; unit/integration tests. | End-to-end capture-to-locked-storage slice; enforced weekly policy; one-day demo cycle configuration; automated rule/state tests.                                         |
| 3             | 3 weeks      | Asynchronous compilation; validation, audio normalization and chronological assembly; retry/failure states; reveal/archive; prompts/reminders; private chat; post-reveal downloads; observability.                      | Working capture-to-reveal workflow; compiled group film; delayed/failure handling; reminders and chat; archive/playback/download.                                         |
| 4             | 2 weeks      | Hardening and defect correction; security/authorization testing; DevSecOps evidence; deployment automation; PWA/native build packaging; five-person pilot; documentation and final demonstration preparation.           | Production-like demo deployment; Android APK and PWA plus iOS build/preview where signing allows; test/security results; usability feedback; final project documentation. |
